text: Hi, my name is Bunlong Heng. I am a Senior Full-Stack Developer with over 12 years of experience building web applications and owning them end to end. I graduated from UMass Lowell with a degree in Computer Science in 2014, and throughout my career I have worked across the entire stack, from React and Node J S to A P I's, databases, cloud, security, and performance. Most recently, I have been working at Thrive. One project I am especially proud of is the Advanced Campaign Editor for the Thrive Business Center. I helped lead and build it using React and Node J S, with backend A P I's and Amazon S three. I also worked heavily on the Reporting Center, including the Keep and Thrive integration, where I helped plan how reporting data should flow between the systems securely and accurately. Performance was a big focus for me there. One of my favorite wins was bringing our dashboard response time down from around five seconds to under half a second. I also worked on observability, security and performance readiness, and mentoring developers. I am A W S certified as both a Solutions Architect Associate and Developer Associate. Lately, though, I have gotten really into auditing. I audit repositories, P R's, Jira epics, and even projects that span multiple repositories. The project I am most excited about is something I built called Repo Audit. Repo Audit reverse-engineers a codebase across ten different engineering lenses, including architecture, security, performance, testing, maintainability, and code quality, and brings everything together into one structured report. I have run more than 500 audits with it so far. But the main reason I built it is actually pretty simple: I want to become a better developer. It lets me go back through my own work, find mistakes, learn from decisions I have made in the past, and bring those lessons into whatever I build next. It also acts as a quality gate. Before I release or open-source something, I can audit it and make sure the code I am putting my name on meets my standards. And as A I gets better, the audits get better too. I can revisit older projects and keep learning from them. That is really how I approach engineering. I love building, I love staying hands-on, and I am always looking for ways to build better software and become a better developer. Thanks for taking the time to learn a little bit about me.
